title: The CapEx Death Spiral: Why Markets Are More Fragile Than You Think
speaker: tastylive panel (hosts not named)

macro_themes.view: Regional banks are levered ~10:1 'Ponzi schemes' facing disruption from AI, DeFi/digital dollars and options-based lending.
Hyperscalers depend on OpenAI and Anthropic, both unprofitable; the whole market is a circular bubble that depends on them.
Hyperscaler debt-funded capex is widening CDS and crowding out the long end; slowing capex would slow earnings and liquidity: a catch-22.
New debt issuance, including hyperscaler borrowing, is a major reason the 10-year yield keeps rising.

calls.reason: Regional banks are 10x levered and their moat is eroding from DeFi, digital dollars and options-based lending; a run would collapse them.
Hyperscaler borrowing crowds out the long end, which is a big reason the 10-year keeps rising.
calls.quote: One of the biggest reasons the 10ear keeps going is because of the total amount of new debt that's being taken.

notes: Panel discussion; no weekday or date stated, so listing date used. No explicit index call: they call the market a bubble but say "markets can stay irrational longer than you can stay solvent". KRE is used as a proxy ticker for "regional banks" and was not named. The TNX bias is an explanation of why yields are rising, read as implying they keep rising.
